seoTitle: How to Use Contact Tags in GoHighLevel (2026)
metaDescription: Add and remove contact tags in GoHighLevel one at a time or in bulk, turn a tag into a self-updating Smart List, and use tags to trigger workflows, including the Apply step that's easy to miss.
intro:
A tag in GoHighLevel (HighLevel) is a label you attach to a contact: vip, follow-up, webinar-2026, anything that helps you find that person again. Tags matter because the rest of the platform keys off them. Smart Lists filter by them, and workflows can start when a tag is added or removed.

This guide covers tagging a single contact, tagging hundreds at once, turning a tag into a Smart List that keeps itself current, and letting workflows do the tagging for you. One detail catches people on the newer contact page: a tag change isn't saved until you confirm it.

steps.heading: Open a contact and find the Tags section
steps.body: Go to Contacts and click a contact's name. The contact detail page puts the person's details in the left panel, conversations and activity in the centre, and modules such as Opportunities, Tasks and Notes on the right. Tags sit in the left panel below Owner and Followers, with a count in brackets. The example contact here, Casey Morgan, shows Tags (2) with high priority and follow-up applied as pills.

image.caption: A contact's detail panel showing two applied tags, high priority and follow-up, just below the owner and followers fields.

steps.heading: Add or remove tags, then click Apply
steps.body:
Open the Tags dropdown and select or deselect tags. To create a new one, type the name and choose the option to add it as a new tag; it becomes available across the whole sub-account straight away.

Then click Apply. HighLevel's documentation for the redesigned contact page is explicit that tag changes are saved only after you confirm them, and Cancel throws them away. Tag-based workflows also fire only once the change is applied. In the recording, the same contact later carries client and vip in place of the original pair, which is the normal pattern: update tags as someone moves from lead to customer so stale labels don't keep them in the wrong lists.

image.caption: The same contact after its tags were changed to client and vip, reflecting a shift from lead status to active customer.

steps.heading: Tag many contacts at once
steps.body:
To tag a group, stay on the Contacts list and tick the checkboxes beside the contacts you want. Click the Add Tag icon in the action bar, give the bulk action a name, choose one or more tags and click Add Tags. Bulk adding appends to each contact's existing tags and never removes any.

Remove Tag works the same way, with a Remove all tags checkbox if you want to wipe every tag from the selection. Large jobs run in the background. Click Check Progress on the confirmation, or open the Bulk Actions tab and use Show Stats to see which contacts were updated.

steps.heading: Filter the Contacts list by tag
steps.body: On the main Contacts screen, click Filters. The panel lists every field you can filter on (Country, Email status, First name, Last email opened date, Owner and many more), and Tags is among them. Choose Tags, pick the tag, and click Apply. You can stack several filters to narrow the segment further, for example tagged vip and email status valid.

image.caption: The Contacts list with the Filters panel open, listing the fields available for building a segment, including contact-level attributes alongside tags.

steps.heading: Save the segment as a Smart List
steps.body:
To keep that segment, use + Add smart list, add the same filters, and click Create. A Smart List isn't a snapshot. It re-evaluates as contacts change, so anyone who gets the vip tag tomorrow joins the list automatically. HighLevel also notes that when an email campaign is scheduled to a Smart List, recipients are worked out at send time.

The flip side is that you can't add people to a Smart List by hand. If someone should be on it, give them the tag.

steps.heading: Let workflows apply and react to tags
steps.body:
In Automation, the Contact Tag trigger starts a workflow when a chosen tag is added to or removed from a contact. The Add Contact Tag and Remove Contact Tag actions do the reverse, so a form submission or booked appointment can tag the contact without anyone touching the record.

Know two behaviours before you build. The trigger isn't retroactive: contacts tagged before the workflow was published won't enter it. And every workflow listening for the same tag fires at once, which can send duplicate messages if two workflows overlap.

troubleshooting.problem: A tag you added disappears when you reopen the contact
troubleshooting.cause: The change was never confirmed. On the redesigned contact page, tag edits are saved only after you click Apply.
troubleshooting.fix: Reopen the Tags dropdown, select the tag again and click Apply before leaving the page.

troubleshooting.problem: A contact received the same message twice after being tagged
troubleshooting.cause: Two published workflows use the same Contact Tag trigger, and HighLevel fires all of them together.
troubleshooting.fix: Merge the logic into one workflow, or give each workflow a different tag.

faq.question: Does bulk tagging overwrite a contact's existing tags?
faq.answer: No. HighLevel's bulk Add Tag action appends the selected tags to whatever the contact already has. Removing tags is a separate Remove Tag bulk action.

faq.question: Can I add someone to a Smart List manually?
faq.answer: No. Smart Lists are built from filters only. To get a contact onto a tag-based Smart List, add the tag to the contact.

faq.question: How many tags should I use?
faq.answer: HighLevel doesn't document a per-contact cap. The practical limit is whether your team uses them consistently. A small agreed set covering lead stage (new-lead, qualified), relationship (client, vip) and action (follow-up) is easier to filter on than dozens of overlapping labels.

faq.question: Can a tag start an automation?
faq.answer: Yes. The Contact Tag workflow trigger fires when a specific tag is added or removed, and the Add Contact Tag and Remove Contact Tag actions let workflows change tags themselves.
